feedback.reason: The request must be compared with all active intervals for its charger after expired holds are excluded. Maintenance notes have no bearing on slot availability.

options.text: Check only whether the requested interval overlaps the reservation being edited.
Use the maintenance-note search index to decide whether the time slot is free.
Lock every charger in the network for each reservation request.
Count expired holds as active until a nightly cleanup job removes them.
Arbitrate the charger’s current reservation intervals together.

questions.prompt: A charging coordinator reserves time on one charger. Reservations must not overlap, and an expired hold frees its interval before a new reservation is accepted. Charger maintenance notes are read-only and may be indexed later. Which boundary should arbitrate a reservation?

constraints: The survivor asset ID stays stable and receives the selected descriptive values.
The retired-ID redirect may be rebuilt later.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The redirect can lag without changing the merged domain asset, so it is not part of the acceptance decision.
details.errorCorrection: Creating a new identity or picking the last stored duplicate contradicts the explicit stable-ID and selection facts.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Keep the survivor identity and selected values together in the merge; rebuild the redirect from the committed result.
details.scenarioApplication: The chosen metadata is written to the stable survivor; a rebuildable redirect can be refreshed from that outcome.
details.transfer: Separate a domain object’s committed values from a derived lookup structure when the latter is explicitly rebuildable.

messages.text: The prompt says the survivor ID remains stable; a new identity would change references for a descriptive correction.
The redirect is explicitly rebuildable later and does not define the survivor’s metadata values.
Only the survivor’s selected values change; unrelated photographs do not participate in this merge.
Storage recency is not the stated selection rule for title and rights values.

feedback.reason: The merge changes descriptive fields on the chosen stable survivor, while the old-ID redirect is a rebuildable projection. Storage recency does not choose the winning metadata.

options.text: Create a new asset identity for each metadata correction and point the survivor to the newest one.
Apply the selected metadata to the stable survivor asset.
Require the redirect projection to update before accepting the metadata merge.
Include every photograph and every redirect in one merge transaction.
Replace the survivor with whichever duplicate record was most recently stored.

questions.prompt: An archive curator merges duplicate metadata for a photograph. The survivor asset ID remains stable; the chosen title and rights statement replace the old values, while the redirect from the retired ID can be rebuilt later. Which state belongs in the merge result?

constraints: A work-territory pair has at most one active approval.
Other territories are independent; audit display may lag.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The display is a projection, and only the specified pair belongs in the consistency scope.
details.errorCorrection: Global uniqueness disallows stated independent approvals; expiry alone does not enforce one active record for the same pair.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The pair-scoped boundary can reject a second active approval without serializing unrelated territory decisions.
details.scenarioApplication: Only approvals for the same work and territory compete for the one active slot.
details.transfer: Derive boundary size from the exact uniqueness key rather than widening it to the whole catalog.

messages.text: The prompt permits independent approvals for other territories, so global uniqueness is broader than the stated rule.
The display may lag, so it cannot reliably arbitrate current active approval state.
Expiry bounds each approval but does not remove the explicit one-active-approval uniqueness requirement.
Only the same work-territory pair participates in uniqueness; unrelated pairs do not need a shared decision.

feedback.reason: Uniqueness is scoped to one work-territory pair, while other territories are explicitly independent and the audit view may lag. The acceptance decision needs only the pair’s active approval state.

options.text: Allow only one active approval for the work across all territories.
Let the audit screen decide whether a new approval is a duplicate.
Accept any number of active approvals and use expiry to choose one at read time.

constraints: Each policy revision is immutable and addressable.

constraints: The domain must not silently grant an unknown status, and reviewers need the raw supplier value.

constraints: A negative feed event is not the same command as a positive repayment; the reference identifies the external event.
A reversal is delivered as a separate negative event.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the bank contract represented reversals with a separate explicit event type, use that marker instead of amount sign.
details.errorCorrection: Absolute value turns a reversal into a repayment; losing the reference removes the stated duplicate check.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Amount direction classifies the event; the bank reference identifies which external event was received.
details.scenarioApplication: A negative event follows the reversal path and can be recognized by its bank reference.
details.transfer: Do not let transport shortcuts erase distinctions between domain operations.

messages.text: Taking an absolute value turns a reversal into a repayment.
A feed DTO’s rounding and field semantics would leak into allocation rules.
Dropping the reference loses the event identity used for deduplication.
Storing a signed delta bypasses the distinct reversal operation and the positive-amount repayment allocation.

feedback.reason: Each feed reference identifies the external event being allocated. The signed amount’s direction distinguishes the two domain commands.

options.text: Take the absolute value of every amount and allocate it as a repayment.
Classify a positive repayment separately from a negative reversal; retain the bank reference.
Pass the bank feed record directly to the account and let it infer whether a negative amount means reversal.
Discard the bank reference after parsing because account balance alone determines duplicate status.
Store the signed bank amount unchanged as the account’s new balance delta.

questions.prompt: In cooperative lending ledger, A bank feed sends repayments as a signed amount, currency, and bank reference. The domain allocation requires a positive Money amount and a unique bank reference; a reversal arrives as a separate negative event. Which boundary decision preserves that contract?

constraints: The timeout transition is state-dependent, and bracket advancement must follow a valid result once.
Timeout is legal only while the match is live.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the tournament explicitly treated all platform timeouts as forfeits regardless of match state, that would change the domain contract.
details.errorCorrection: Mapping timeout straight to forfeit ignores the live-state precondition; advancing first can publish an invalid bracket.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A provider status describes an event; only the match state determines whether that event is a legal transition.
details.scenarioApplication: A timeout advances a live match once, while the domain rejects it in any other state.
details.transfer: Normalize external status labels but keep legal transitions in the state-owning domain.

messages.text: A timeout on a non-live match would create an invalid transition.
This publishes the next bracket slot before the state-checked result operation can reject an illegal transition.
Letting each caller decide advancement creates multiple owners for the same bracket transition rule.
A timeout must not be reclassified as a forfeit without the domain rule.

feedback.reason: A valid result advances the bracket once. The operation checks both the match state and the result transition.

options.text: Map timeout directly to forfeited for any match because the platform reports a timeout.
Let the platform DTO update the next bracket slot before the domain validates the match state.
Translate the status and invoke the state-checked match result operation.
Add every platform status label to the bracket domain and let each caller decide which advance.
Treat every platform timeout as a completed forfeit and publish the next bracket slot immediately.

questions.prompt: In tournament bracket service, An event platform sends match outcomes using its own status labels. The bracket recognizes only completed, forfeited, or pending; a timeout is valid only from a live match, and the result advances the bracket once. Which boundary decision preserves that contract?

constraints: Classification is evidence; refund eligibility is a distinct policy decision.
Refund eligibility is a separate policy decision.
The return record retains the scanner observation used to explain each refund-eligibility decision.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the business explicitly authorized a calibrated score threshold as its refund rule, that threshold would need to be stated and owned.
details.errorCorrection: Confidence is not stated as approval, and combining classification with payment collapses distinct meanings.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A scanner observation describes condition; refund eligibility is a separate authorization decision.
details.scenarioApplication: The saved return retains the scanner observation, while the return policy separately evaluates eligibility.
details.transfer: Map observations as evidence rather than turning them into an unstated business outcome.

messages.text: Confidence is not authorization to refund.
The scanner’s classification vocabulary is not the refund rule.
Without the observed condition, the saved refund cannot be traced back to the scanner evidence used for eligibility.
Confidence measures the scanner’s certainty; the case does not make it the refund amount.

feedback.reason: The scanner confidence score describes the observation, not approval. Evidence and eligibility remain distinct inputs to the return decision.

options.text: Treat a high scanner confidence score as the domain’s refund decision.
Use the scanner label directly as a refund enum so one value drives both classification and payment.
Discard the observed condition after calculating eligibility because only the refund amount is stored.
Let the classifier’s confidence score directly set the refund amount.
Record scanner labels as evidence; evaluate refund eligibility with the return policy.

questions.prompt: In returns inspection workflow, A warehouse scanner labels an item as `damaged`, `opened`, or `unused`. The domain separately decides classification and refund eligibility; the scanner’s confidence value is not an approval. Which boundary decision preserves that contract?

constraints: The result must identify exact inputs, while the latest tag can point elsewhere later.
The “latest” tag may point to a different revision later.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the “latest” tag were immutable by contract, it could be retained as the exact input identity.
details.errorCorrection: A mutable tag does not identify a reproducible input; a display title cannot recover missing lineage.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Mutable aliases locate inputs but cannot identify the exact revisions used by a published result.
details.scenarioApplication: Reviewers can retrieve the dataset and code revisions that the result actually used.
details.transfer: Convert temporary external references into the stable identities the domain publication contract requires.

messages.text: A mutable tag cannot reproduce which dataset was used.
A URI field can locate data but does not say which immutable revision the result used.
A title plus omitted provenance gives reviewers no dataset or code revision to retrieve.
Resolving `latest` during each audit can return different inputs from those used at publication.

feedback.reason: Reviewers must be able to retrieve the exact inputs used for publication. The published result names fixed inputs rather than mutable runner aliases.

options.text: Resolve both handles to immutable dataset and code revisions before publishing provenance.
Store only the latest tag so the publisher can always fetch the current inputs.
Copy the runner response wholesale into the domain result and make its URI fields the result identity.
Store the result’s displayed title and omit dataset/code provenance because the runner can be queried later.
Keep only a reproducible URL string and resolve its `latest` target during every audit.

questions.prompt: In research-notebook platform, A notebook runner reports a dataset URI, code commit, and a mutable “latest” tag. A published result must identify the exact dataset and code revisions used so another reviewer can retrieve those inputs. Which boundary decision preserves that contract?

constraints: The accepted comment must retain author and exact revision, and notification is a separate effect.
The submitted revision is checked when the comment is accepted.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If markup itself were the agreed comment domain language, retaining it could be correct.
details.errorCorrection: Rendering raw transport markup leaks presentation policy; substituting current revision changes what the author reviewed.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Comment content, author identity, revision precondition, and notification status have different meanings.
details.scenarioApplication: The comment is accepted against the submitted revision; notification remains a separate post-acceptance effect.
details.transfer: Map client representations at entry while preserving the domain facts needed to accept and identify the comment.

messages.text: Storing markdown as the domain value couples comment semantics to the provider format.
The submitted token is the precondition; accepting against the current revision would bypass a stale-token conflict.
Notification delivery status is not part of comment content and cannot change the comment’s acceptance.
Recording the submitted token as an attribute does not make a comment on the current revision satisfy the token precondition.

feedback.reason: Notification is a separate effect after the comment decision. The stored comment has plain text and stable identities; rendering remains outside the incoming API shape.

options.text: Store raw markdown in the comment entity and render it whenever the comment is read.
Accept comments against the current document revision even when the client submitted a different revision token.
Put notification delivery status into the comment value so the domain can retry the API call.
Map markdown, author identity, and revision into the comment; notify only after acceptance.
Accept against the current revision and record the client revision as a comment attribute.

questions.prompt: In collaborative annotation workspace, A comment API accepts markdown and a document revision token. The domain stores plain text, author identity, and exact revision; notification is a separate effect after acceptance. Which boundary decision preserves that contract?

constraints: The list needs counts only, not reservation objects.
The operator never opens reservation records from the capacity screen.
The capacity-screen read path has a two-query and 1 MB transfer budget; all reservation rows for these stations total 80 MB.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If operators could inspect individual reservations inline, a bounded detail load for the selected station would be warranted.
details.errorCorrection: Loading the full reservation rows sends 80 MB through a path capped at 1 MB; per-station reads also exceed the two-query budget.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A read projection can calculate an aggregate without materializing the related entities.
details.scenarioApplication: The count projection stays within the 1 MB and two-query limits; materializing the reservation graph or issuing one query per station does not.
details.transfer: Match the query shape to fields the caller consumes; do not fetch a relationship merely because it exists.

messages.text: The full reservation rows total 80 MB, far above the screen’s 1 MB transfer budget.
Per-row lazy reads exceed the two-query budget for the screen.
Loading the reservation graph exceeds the stated 1 MB transfer budget and adds unrelated relationships.
One count query per station exceeds the two-query budget.

feedback.reason: A scalar count is the consumed information; transferring reservation objects adds data this response never uses. Because reservation details are never opened here, the row can show its count without transferring child records.

options.text: Load every reservation for all 40 stations and count them in the screen.
Lazy-load reservations as each count is rendered.
Load all station, reservation, charger, and maintenance relationships into one graph.
Issue a separate count query for every station after fetching the station page.
Project each station with its active-reservation count.

questions.prompt: In fleet charging coordinator, The capacity screen lists 40 stations and shows each station’s active reservation count. The operator never opens reservation records from this screen. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: The page is limited to 25 plot rows but needs the gardener name on each row.
The page contains at most 25 plots.
The page may read at most 25 plots and has a two-query budget; all 25 gardeners are distinct and uncached, and this loader issues one query per lazy access without batching.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the list omitted gardener names, the plot page could be returned without loading gardeners.
details.errorCorrection: Reading all plots exceeds the 25-row request bound; this loader’s uncached per-gardener reads exceed the page’s two-query budget.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A page boundary limits the root records whose related values belong in the response.
details.scenarioApplication: The page query returns no more than 25 plots with only their gardener names, within the two-query budget.
details.transfer: For paged results, constrain relationship loading to the selected page or project only the needed fields.

messages.text: Reading every plot before taking the page exceeds the 25-row read bound.
This case’s loader issues 25 separate reads for the 25 distinct uncached gardeners, exceeding the two-query budget.
Loading both complete sets ignores the page boundary and transfers unnecessary data.
Twenty-five independent gardener requests exceed the page’s two-query budget.

feedback.reason: The page boundary limits which gardener records belong to the response; loading the whole garden ignores that scope. Only gardeners associated with the returned plot page are needed to build these rows.

options.text: Fetch gardener names for only the 25 plots in the requested page.
Load all plots with gardeners, then take the first 25 in memory.
Use lazy gardener access while rendering each row.
Fetch every gardener and every plot, then join the page in application memory.
Fetch gardener names after rendering the page through 25 independent requests.

questions.prompt: In community garden allocation tool, A weekly plot list displays gardener names for 200 plots. The gardener name is required on every row; the page must stay at 25 plots per request. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: The report consumes two aggregates, not annotation entities.
The report does not display annotation text or author profiles.
The report data-access contract allows at most 1 MB of materialized rows per request; for this quarter, full annotation rows total 80 MB and timestamp-only rows total 4 MB.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the report later needs individual annotation text, it should use a separate detail query.
details.errorCorrection: Full annotation rows total 80 MB and timestamp-only rows total 4 MB, each over the 1 MB materialization cap; the report needs only two aggregates.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Aggregate queries return measures without creating annotation objects or loading their fields.
details.scenarioApplication: Database aggregation returns only count and latest time, while loading annotation rows or timestamps into the service exceeds the stated transfer cap.
details.transfer: Projection is appropriate when a read caller needs a summary rather than domain relationships.

messages.text: Materializing full annotation rows would return 80 MB, above the 1 MB report data-access limit.
Lazy iteration still materializes annotation rows and exceeds the 1 MB data-access limit.
Grouping by author splits an episode’s measures into several groups, but the report requires one count and latest time per episode.
Timestamp-only rows total 4 MB, above the 1 MB materialization limit.

feedback.reason: Counts and latest times are aggregates, so annotation entities do not contribute fields the report needs. The returned report consists of two measures rather than annotation content.

options.text: Load every annotation and compute both values in application code.
Expose a lazy annotations collection to the report and aggregate it row by row.
Group by episode and author, then report each episode-author group as the episode total.
Group by episode to return annotation count and latest time.
Load annotation count in SQL but read every annotation to find the latest timestamp.

questions.prompt: In podcast production desk, An archive report needs the number of annotations per episode and the latest annotation time. It does not display annotation text or author profiles. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: The export needs the approver name, and deferred reads would occur after the transaction closes.
Serialization and upload happen after the scoped database context closes; no database access is allowed afterward.
The read transaction closes before the external upload starts, whose duration is unbounded.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the upload were performed inside a streaming database scope by design, resource lifetime would need an explicit separate decision.
details.errorCorrection: The export contract requires the read transaction to close before the unbounded external upload; deferred reads after closure cannot supply approver names.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Deferred relationship access is unsafe when serialization occurs outside the read scope.
details.scenarioApplication: Approver names must already be present before transaction close because the upload begins only after that boundary.
details.transfer: Make required relationship access explicit before the data-access scope closes; avoid hidden I/O during serialization.

messages.text: Deferred access can attempt I/O after the bounded read scope is gone.
The contract requires closing the read transaction before this unbounded external upload.
The export must include approver names before its bounded read transaction closes.

feedback.reason: The serializer runs after the bounded transaction, so a deferred name read cannot satisfy the export. Each export row must already include the approver name at transaction close.

options.text: Return grant entities with deferred approver loads and serialize them after closing the transaction.
Return approver names before the bounded read transaction closes.
Keep the transaction open while an external file upload serializes the object graph.
Detach the grants and allow the serializer to issue a fresh principal query later.

questions.prompt: In permissions review service, An audit export loads grant rows inside a scoped read transaction. Each exported row includes the approver’s display name. Serialization and an external upload occur after the database context closes; no database access is allowed afterward. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: Every current grant and expiry is displayed, and the child set has a small stated cap.
The current grant set is capped at 12 rows.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the grant set were unbounded or only a subset were displayed, a separate paged query could be preferable.
details.errorCorrection: Deferred loads add hidden reads for fields guaranteed to be shown.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A bounded child collection can be materialized when the caller consumes all of it.
details.scenarioApplication: The selected title view displays all 12 current grants and their expiry dates.
details.transfer: Eagerly load relationships that the caller always consumes when their size and scope are bounded.

messages.text: Deferred loads add hidden reads for fields guaranteed to be shown.
Usage histories exceed the detail contract; the cap applies to grants only.
One request per grant duplicates access coordination despite the bounded set.
All grants and expiries are shown in one short detail request.

feedback.reason: The selected view consumes the complete but explicitly capped grant set during one request. The twelve-row cap makes the complete grant detail part of this selected-principal response.

options.text: Return a title proxy and fetch grants only when each row is painted.
Load every territory record and all usage histories for the title.
Load the title and its capped grant set with expiries for this detail view.
Return only the title and make the screen issue an independent request for each grant expiry.
Fetch the grant expiries in a separate request for each displayed grant.

questions.prompt: In digital rights clearance tool, A title detail screen always shows the title, its current territory grants, and each grant expiry. The set is capped at 12 rows and is read in one short request. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: The report uses a date, while the large notes are a separate selected-aircraft detail.
Service notes are large and opened only for a selected aircraft.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If replacement date must be derived from note history, the query should state that bounded aggregate explicitly.
details.errorCorrection: Eager loading transfers large optional notes for every aircraft.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Separating list and detail shapes avoids carrying large payloads for unselected rows.
details.scenarioApplication: The fleet report keeps each aircraft’s date; notes arrive only after selection.
details.transfer: Do not make an optional large relationship part of every list read.

messages.text: Eager loading transfers large optional notes for every aircraft.
A lazy proxy makes presentation code trigger I/O implicitly.
Scanning all notes is unnecessary if the replacement date is already the report field.
The report already has a replacement date field, and note history is optional detail.

feedback.reason: The large notes belong to a later user action and should not burden the fleet summary. Opening a particular aircraft is the only action that consumes its large service notes.

options.text: Eager-load every battery note for every aircraft in the report.
Give the report a lazy note proxy and let row formatting decide whether to fetch notes.
Read every service note to find the next replacement date, then discard the notes.
Add a database trigger that copies every note into the report table whenever any note changes.
Project the next replacement date; read service notes after an aircraft is selected.

questions.prompt: In drone maintenance planner, A weekly fleet report shows aircraft ID and the next battery replacement date. Battery service notes are large and opened only after an operator selects one aircraft. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: Capacity is the only required related value; patient data is outside this screen.
Patient referrals and notes are outside this directory screen.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If capacity were not persisted and had to be calculated from active referrals, a controlled aggregate query would be needed.
details.errorCorrection: The broad load carries data outside the stated display contract.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A projection can include one required related scalar without traversing unrelated relationships.
details.scenarioApplication: Clinic capacity appears without retrieving referral or medical-note records.
details.transfer: Keep query ownership aligned with the read contract and exclude unrelated sensitive relationships.

messages.text: The broad load carries data outside the stated display contract.
An unconsumed lazy relationship still leaves a hidden I/O path in UI code.
The renderer should not calculate a domain summary by reading all patient notes.
The directory requires a focused capacity value, not patient notes or row-by-row UI queries.

feedback.reason: Capacity is the only related value this directory consumes; patient records add unrelated data. The directory can display capacity without fetching patient-side relationships.

options.text: Project clinic identity and capacity without referral or patient-note data.
Eager-load all referrals and patient notes so capacity can be recalculated in memory.
Expose lazy referrals and rely on the UI not to iterate them.
Load all medical notes and count active referrals for every clinic in the renderer.
Use a correlated patient-note subquery in the UI for every directory row.

questions.prompt: In clinic referral coordinator, A specialist directory lists 80 clinics. Each clinic row needs its current capacity value, but patient referrals and medical notes must not be fetched on this screen. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: Only 30 meter rows and one current owner name per row are needed.
This dashboard endpoint permits at most two database reads per request: the meter page and one related-data read.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If each row also showed full owner history, that relationship would need its own explicit bounded access plan.
details.errorCorrection: One hidden lookup per row scales query count with the rendered list.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Batching related values keeps read count independent of the number of parent rows.
details.scenarioApplication: The 30 owner names fit in the single related-data read allowed for this refresh.
details.transfer: Batch related values for a known set of roots when a list consumes the same small relationship from each.

messages.text: One hidden lookup per row scales query count with the rendered list.
The full-region join ignores the selected 30-row scope.
Histories and reservations are not part of the dashboard fields.
A page-wide batch is needed to avoid the repeated owner lookup.

feedback.reason: Thirty separate owner reads would exceed the endpoint’s stated two-read budget. The thirty owner values fit in the one related-data read allowed after the meter page.

options.text: Lazy-load each owner as the dashboard paints meter rows.
Load every owner and every meter in the region, then combine them in the dashboard.
Load complete owner histories and all meter reservations for each displayed meter.
Fetch owner names in one batch for the 30 meter IDs.
Run one owner query per meter row, but cache the result only for this render.

questions.prompt: In neighborhood energy-sharing service, A dashboard lists 30 meters with the next reserved window. It also shows each meter’s current owner name. The owner table is shared, and the dashboard refreshes once per request. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: The skill labels are needed for all rows, but the root page is bounded.
This page contract permits at most two database reads, regardless of its 20-row maximum.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If only selected volunteers’ skills were shown, an explicit detail read after selection would be smaller.
details.errorCorrection: Repeated per-assignment reads make query count grow with the page.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A bounded page can fetch related labels in a fixed read budget rather than per-row.
details.scenarioApplication: Adding assignments to a page does not add database round trips for their skill labels.
details.transfer: Choose a batch or projection when a bounded page consumes the same relation across its rows.

messages.text: Repeated per-assignment reads make query count grow with the page.
The full directory and availability graph are outside the shift page.
A proxy hides relationship I/O in view rendering.
The page needs every row’s labels, so per-row conditional reads do not fit its contract.

feedback.reason: A per-assignment query makes the number of reads grow with page rows, contrary to the request cap. The shift page can return its row labels without increasing reads as assignments are added.

options.text: Run a new skill query for every assignment while building the page.
Fetch skill labels for the assignment page in one scoped read.
Load the entire volunteer directory with every assignment and availability record.
Add skills to a lazy volunteer proxy and let the page renderer trigger them.
Load one volunteer’s skills only after its row is expanded, even though every row displays the labels.

questions.prompt: In volunteer coordination hub, A shift page shows assignments for one shift and the volunteers’ skill labels. Each page contains at most 20 assignments; there is no filtering by skill. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: The list needs only IDs and dataset revision; the large log belongs to selected detail.
The execution log may be several megabytes.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the list needed a small log status, project that status rather than the complete log.
details.errorCorrection: The logs are large and not read on the list screen.
details.mechanismOrProperty: List and detail queries can select different columns according to their callers.
details.scenarioApplication: The large log is absent from search rows and fetched only for an opened result.
details.transfer: Split summary and detail reads when their relationship sizes and access patterns differ.

messages.text: The logs are large and not read on the list screen.
A lazy proxy leaves UI access responsible for triggering database reads.
Loading before paging transfers the full dataset and undermines the page request.
Omitting logs after fetching them does not avoid the unnecessary transfer and materialization.

feedback.reason: The list and detail consume different amounts of data; fetching a megabyte log for each list row has no caller benefit. Experiment ID and dataset revision identify a list row; the execution log belongs to result detail.

options.text: Eager-load all execution logs for every result in the list.
Attach a lazy log proxy to each row and let the UI open it on demand.
Project list fields and load the large execution log on result detail.
Load every result, dataset, source file, and execution log before paging.
Fetch logs for all results but strip them from the JSON response.

questions.prompt: In research-notebook platform, A result list displays experiment ID and dataset revision. Opening a result shows code commit and execution log. The log may be several megabytes. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: This workflow uses all of one selected return’s bounded evidence before completing its decision.
The decision is submitted before the read scope ends.
The complete selection-to-decision evidence read has a one-query budget; no follow-up reads are allowed before submission.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If photo count were unbounded, the workflow would need a bounded evidence page rather than an unrestricted eager load.
details.errorCorrection: The evidence flow permits one read; a selected-return query followed by separate relationship reads would exceed that contract.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Evidence needed for a decision must be available before the bounded read scope ends.
details.scenarioApplication: The one-query evidence read makes the selected return’s photos and history available before the decision is submitted.
details.transfer: Load the relationships a decision requires, scoped to the selected root and its stated bounds.

messages.text: Deferred reads can occur outside the stated data scope.
Separate relationship reads require follow-up queries after selecting the return, violating the one-query evidence contract.
The decision uses both evidence sets before its request completes.

feedback.reason: The decision uses the evidence before the bounded read scope ends, so deferred access is too late. The inspector has the selected return evidence while deciding, before leaving the read scope.

options.text: Return a return proxy and fetch each photo when it is drawn, after the read scope closes.
Return only the return ID and make the decision handler reread each relationship separately.
Return photo IDs but defer photo content and classification history until after the decision.
Load the selected return’s photos and classification history before its decision.

questions.prompt: In returns inspection workflow, An inspector views one return and always needs its inspection photos and classification history. The screen submits a decision before the read scope ends. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: The search result consumes only three fields and opens text separately.
Notice text is opened on a separate page.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a search snippet were required, project only that bounded snippet.
details.errorCorrection: Eagerly loading bodies and attachments carries unneeded data.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A result projection avoids loading fields that belong to a later user action.
details.scenarioApplication: Search rows carry notice ID, effective time, and platform; body text stays on the notice page.
details.transfer: Select only data the caller uses and keep large detail behind an explicit read.

messages.text: Eagerly loading bodies and attachments carries unneeded data.
Lazy loading in rendering can create extra reads for visible rows.
Filtering a large graph after transfer does not reduce database or network work.
The search list does not consume bodies; fetching them per row is still needless work.

feedback.reason: The search response does not need the body that a separate page displays. Notice text is absent from search and is fetched only on the separate notice page.

options.text: Project notice ID, effective time, and platform for search results.
Eager-load every notice body and attachment for all matching routes.
Use a lazy notice-text relationship when the list renders each result.
Return the entire route-notice graph and remove unused fields in the UI.
Fetch notice bodies in a second query per visible search result.

questions.prompt: In public-transit disruption board, An operator search returns route and service-day matches. The display needs notice ID, effective time, and platform only; notice text is opened on a separate page. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: The edit uses current metadata; rendition history is a separate optional view.
The edit form does not display historical renditions.
Current metadata for the selected asset is 12 KB; its rendition history is 80 MB, and the edit request has a 1 MB data-transfer budget.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If an edit action depended on a specific historical rendition, that revision should be loaded explicitly before the action.
details.errorCorrection: The 80 MB rendition history exceeds the edit request’s 1 MB transfer budget; the current metadata edit does not need that payload.
details.mechanismOrProperty: An edit query can load current values without traversing historical versions.
details.scenarioApplication: The current metadata fits the 1 MB edit request; fetching the 80 MB rendition history during that request exceeds its transfer budget.
details.transfer: Load the current aggregate state needed for an operation and keep optional history as an explicit query.

messages.text: Loading rendition data for the collection includes the 80 MB history, above the edit request’s 1 MB transfer budget.
Evaluating the proxy transfers the 80 MB history in a request limited to 1 MB, before the optional history view is opened.
Re-reading the 80 MB rendition history during a 1 MB metadata edit exceeds the request budget.
Caching the 80 MB rendition collection when the form opens exceeds the edit request’s 1 MB budget.

feedback.reason: Current metadata is sufficient for this edit; historical renditions are not part of the form. The edit uses current descriptive values; no historical rendition is displayed or changed.

options.text: Eager-load every rendition and its metadata for all assets in the collection.
Evaluate a lazy rendition-history proxy while building the edit form, transferring its full history before the optional history view is opened.
Re-query the asset and all renditions after every field change.
Load current metadata for editing; query rendition history only when opened.
Copy the whole rendition collection into a cache when the edit form opens.

questions.prompt: In photo-archive curation tool, An archivist edits one asset’s descriptive values while preserving stable asset identity. The edit form shows the asset and current metadata but does not display every historical rendition. Which read plan fits this caller?

constraints: The selected principal has a bounded active-grant set and every expiry is displayed.
This detail request permits at most two database reads for the selected principal.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the grant count were unbounded, paginate the grant view instead of loading all rows.
details.errorCorrection: Per-grant loads repeat access for each displayed permission.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A selected-principal boundary limits which grants and expiry values the query needs.
details.scenarioApplication: Only that principal’s at-most-ten active grants appear in the detail response.
details.transfer: Scope relationship loading to the selected entity and the exact fields the caller uses.

messages.text: Per-grant loads repeat access for each displayed permission.
Other principals and complete audit histories are outside this view.
A second lookup per grant adds hidden round trips for a field already required.
The relationship query should be scoped before transfer to the selected principal.

feedback.reason: The detail request shows a bounded set for one principal; unrelated grants and principals do not affect it. The response contains active grant expiries for one selected principal within its two-read budget.

options.text: Lazy-load grants one at a time as the access screen checks each permission.
Fetch the selected principal and active grants with expiries in one related-data read.
Load every role grant and audit event for all principals.
Fetch role names only and make the screen query expiry separately for each grant.

details.scenarioApplication: A newer revision provides the case that can falsify an implicit “latest is selected” assumption.
details.transfer: Use tests that separate two values the current happy path happens to make equal.

messages.text: The test never creates a newer revision after selection, so it cannot support that equivalence.
The signature call does not show which bytes or revision were sealed.
That changes the operation and does not prove the requested selected revision is the one identified.
A second confirmation does not itself bind the seal to a stable revision identity.

feedback.reason: The current test cannot distinguish selected revision from latest because they never diverge. The review should request a counterexample where a newer revision appears before sealing.

options.text: Treat latest and selected revision as equivalent because they match in the test.
Document only the signature call and omit the selected revision binding.
Test a newer revision appearing after selection but before sealing.
Seal all revisions to avoid choosing the wrong one.
Ask the user to confirm the latest revision again without retaining its identity.

questions.prompt: A document service seals a selected revision before archival. What evidence should the review request?

constraints: A payout release is tied to a settled order and uses a stable request key. After a timeout, the processor may have accepted the request; no lookup behavior is specified.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the processor documents a lookup or deduplication result, record that guarantee and test the corresponding retry path.
details.errorCorrection: The missing lookup contract is an explicit question for the integration owner.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The record separates the application’s stable-key behavior from the processor’s unspecified timeout semantics.
details.scenarioApplication: A retry with a new key risks duplicating a release that was accepted before the timeout.
details.transfer: State what is known and leave external-effect guarantees open until verified.

messages.text: The case gives a request key but no processor guarantee about deduplication or lookup after timeout.
A new key could represent a second release while the first request may already have been accepted.
The prompt explicitly says acceptance may have occurred before the timeout.
A manual-only process is a broad operational choice before the missing processor behavior is clarified.

feedback.reason: The stable request key describes the retry intent, but timeout leaves the effect unknown and the processor lookup contract is absent. The review must not promise exactly-once behavior from the key alone.

options.text: State that the stable key guarantees exactly one payout despite the timeout.
Confirm timeout lookup semantics before claiming stable-key retries are safe.
Recommend retrying with a new key so a timed-out request cannot block progress.
Treat every timeout as a rejection and record no uncertainty.
Require staff to inspect every payout manually without checking whether a processor lookup exists.

questions.prompt: A marketplace releases seller payouts after settlement. How should the review describe an uncertain processor response?

constraints: Passengers must see changes in effective-time order. The operator can send a delayed earlier change after a newer one; the current test sends updates in order.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the operator later guarantees ordered delivery, record and verify that upstream contract rather than assume it.
details.errorCorrection: Choosing a queue is premature because the ordering requirement can be evaluated independently of that mechanism.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Effective time, not arrival time, is the ordering property passengers rely on.
details.scenarioApplication: The counterexample separates the two clocks and tests the actual contract.
details.transfer: Use a review example that distinguishes the proposed rule from a plausible competing interpretation.

messages.text: Ordered test input cannot establish behavior when a delayed earlier effective time arrives later.
Receive time can conflict with the passenger-visible effective-time contract.
A queue is a proposed mechanism, not the missing evidence about ordering semantics.
A late message may carry an earlier effective change that passengers still must see in order.

feedback.reason: The existing test makes receive and effective order identical, so it cannot validate the stated ordering contract. The review needs the delayed earlier event case before asserting the behavior.

options.text: Test a delayed earlier effective time before claiming the board preserves order.
Say arrival order is adequate because all current tests send updates in order.
Record receive timestamp as the ordering source to simplify processing.
Mandate a distributed queue before establishing the delayed-update behavior.
Ignore any update that arrives late without recording whether it is still effective.

questions.prompt: A transit board receives platform changes from an operator. What should the review make clear about event ordering?

constraints: A meter cannot hold overlapping reservations. The normal reservation path passes; no test injects a failure between checking overlap and recording the reservation.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the test reproduces the race, choose and document a mechanism that matches the actual persistence boundary.
details.errorCorrection: A cleanup job would permit the forbidden overlap before repairing it.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A failure/interleaving test can show whether two overlapping reservations are possible at the check-record boundary.
details.scenarioApplication: The prompt does not identify the store or process scope, so a specific lock prescription is unsupported.
details.transfer: Review evidence should target the untested state transition, not repeat the already-passing path.

messages.text: A successful normal request does not exercise an interleaving or a failure between check and record.
The mechanism cannot be selected from the stated facts; first establish the failure behavior and owning store.
That violates the immediate no-overlap contract and creates a known invalid state.
Repeated sequential execution does not create the specified check/record interleaving.

feedback.reason: The case’s gap is between overlap validation and reservation recording. The review should preserve the invariant and request a test that exercises that boundary rather than claim atomicity or choose an unsupported lock.

options.text: Declare the reservation atomic because the normal request test passes.
Mandate a database lock without knowing the persistence boundary.
Allow overlaps and plan to resolve them in a later cleanup job.
Run the existing normal case many times and infer concurrency safety from no observed error.
Exercise a failure between overlap check and reservation record before claiming concurrent safety.

questions.prompt: An energy-sharing service reserves meter discharge windows. Which review action addresses the unresolved failure mode?

constraints: The new provider has a different request format. Existing consumers rely on the current timing and error contract; no compatibility test has run against the new provider.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If that test shows a timing or error difference, record the accepted tradeoff or revise the integration before rollout.
details.errorCorrection: A provider-specific test can compare the response behavior with the existing contract.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The adapter is intended to isolate the new request format while consumers keep the existing contract.
details.scenarioApplication: Compilation covers type/syntax compatibility, not observed timing or error behavior.
details.transfer: Do not communicate an integration guarantee until the relevant behavior is measured.

messages.text: Compilation does not establish the new provider’s timing or error behavior.
This moves provider-specific format changes into consumers that depend on the existing contract.
A format difference can be translated at the boundary; the facts do not establish that the provider must change.
No compatibility or timing test has run, so zero added latency is unsupported.

feedback.reason: The adapter compiles, but no test establishes that the new provider preserves the stream’s timing and error contract. The review should make that acceptance boundary explicit and request evidence.

options.text: State that the contract is preserved because the adapter compiles.
Ask every consumer to handle the new provider’s response format.
Reject the provider until it adopts the existing request format.
Run a provider-specific test against the existing timing and error contract.
Promise that translation adds no timing cost without measuring it.

familyConfig.brief: Model the domain for a library loan service. A member may borrow eligible copies, return or renew a loan, and incur a hold when no copy is available. The system must preserve loan limits and prevent the same physical copy from being actively loaned twice. Describe behavior and ownership without assuming a particular language or persistence technology.

reviewCriteria.description: Clarify member eligibility, copy availability, renewal rules, holds, and the invariants that must always hold.
Assign state and behavior to domain concepts and explain the collaboration for borrow, return, and renewal.
Discuss invariant ownership, concurrency, extension points, and the cost of alternative responsibility boundaries.
Summarize the core model, protected invariants, major tradeoffs, and a useful validation step.
